note: Judge 2026-09-30 (cont 5). The prior weak (Code and Identifier unproven) is closed and was a real defect: an Access-Challenge carrying EAP Code 0 was handed to the peer and answered. Fix in processEAPMessage pins Code 1 for an Access-Challenge only (Accept/Reject may carry Success/Failure), and new checkEAPResponseHeader requires Code 2 and the current Request's Identifier before forwarding; RFC 3579 Section 2.2 quotes above both, text checked. Length: the existing corruptEAPFrom pair. Code, server side: negative TestRFC3579NASRefusesANonRequestCodeInAChallenge rewrites only the Code octet (0,2,3,4,5,255) and asserts the infrastructure error naming the server's EAP header, not ErrAuthRejected, and exactly one Access-Request (nothing forwarded). Code+Identifier, peer side: positive TestRFC3579NASForwardsTheCurrentIdentifierBothWays pairs every Challenge's Request with the next Access-Request's Response (Code 2, same Identifier) over a full EAP-MSCHAPv2 login and the check admits a matching pair; negative TestRFC3579NASRefusesAResponseOffTheCurrentIdentifier drives checkEAPResponseHeader directly (Identifier 6/8 vs 7, Code 1, Code 4), since the in-process peer echoes the Identifier and cannot be driven off it. Ze ends the login on a mismatched Response rather than silently discarding it; with an in-process peer no other Response can arrive, so nothing is forwarded either way. Valid EAP-TLS/MSCHAPv2 flows stay green (race run 2026-09-30). All units recorded red.
